title: Learned network models nominate two cancer-drug combinations for laboratory follow-up
summary: A transfer-learning framework combining learned drug and disease representations with biological-network propagation nominated two drug combinations. The paper reports laboratory growth-inhibition synergy for the selected cancer-cell models. This is a preclinical candidate result, not demonstrated treatment efficacy in patients.
ai_technology: Graph isomorphism network embeddings; fully connected neural networks; transfer learning

evidence.tested: The case study links learned drug-disease scores and a refined combination model to selection of two combinations for laboratory assessment.
evidence.unknown: No clinical efficacy, safety, independently replicated mechanism or broad generalization is established. Many additional network/pathway predictions are computational only and are outside the represented result. The model description contains inconsistent optimizer-setting statements. Operational experimental procedures were not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Learned molecular embeddings and neural interaction models contribute to combination nomination; deterministic network propagation is only one component of the hybrid workflow.

source_review.scope: Exact primary front tuple, computational embedding/model/selection Methods and nonactionable case-study result. Operational assays excluded.
